text:
evan: Heads-up — found a reproducible KV cache paging regression hitting staging when we run long-context PagedAttention workloads. Memory climbs steadily and then we get a big stall while evicting; looks like pagetable fragmentation + repeated pagewalk retries.

zoe: Can you paste the short logs and the exact repro command?

evan: Repro command I used:
```
./repro_kv_pager --model=gptx-small --seq=32 --longseq=8192 --batch=4 --arch=h100 --enable-pagedattn
```
Minimal log excerpt (sanitized):
```
2025-07-12T15:02:01Z kvcache: alloc_page pid=2341 seq=8192 idx=1234
2025-07-12T15:02:01Z kvcache: map_pt entry=0x7f9a retry=0 owner=0x3
2025-07-12T15:02:02Z kvcache: pagewalk retry=5 owner=0x3 status=EVICTED
2025-07-12T15:02:02Z kvcache: evict_async queued_count=32
gpu_kernel_launch_time_ms: [0.21, 0.19, 1.91, 3.44, 0.22]
```
Pattern: slow kernel launches spike right after repeated pagewalk retries, and then eviction queue drains very slowly.

ajay: Interesting — I ran the same repro on MI250X and the growth pattern is similar but the stall looks like a synchronous wait in the pager thread (roc profiler shows CPU spinning on a cond var). Not exactly same kernel-time spikes but overall throughput drops 8-12x.

rachel: Could this be interaction with the kernel selection path? When tiled kernels (tiling_v1) are chosen we allocate bigger per-page metadata, perhaps increasing fragmentation under longctx.

evan: I tried forcing tiling_v2 kernels via env var and it reduced the large stalls but the memory still keeps growing slowly until we finally OOM the worker. So two separate things: kernel layout affecting fragmentation, and a pager/pathological eviction ordering that doesn't reclaim effectively.

zoe: Can you dump the pagetable occupancy histogram? We added that metric recently.

evan: Here's a quick snapshot (from the run):
```
pt_hist: {0-4k: 128, 4k-64k: 512, 64k-256k: 4096, 256k-1M: 1024, >1M: 48}
free_runs_without_reclaim: 23
evict_retry_backoff_ms: [0, 10, 20, 40, 80]
```
Looks like lots of mid-size fragments that never coalesce.

ajay: On MI profiling I also see repeated page descriptors being reissued with different owners (owner id flips between kernel threads) which matches "map_pt entry owner churn". Could be stale owner bookkeeping causing a failed coalesce path.

sre-bot: perf-test scheduled: kvcache-pager/longctx/h100 (auto-run id=pt-20250712-3).

rachel: Two action hypotheses: (1) pager's coalesce pass only runs on full-evict, but under steady longctx it never reaches threshold; we should trigger periodic background coalesce/compaction. (2) owner churn + kernel selection leads to small lifetime windows that prevent reuse, so lowering reuse_window or throttling kernel migration might help.

evan: Agreed. I'll add an experimental compaction trigger after N allocations and instrument reclaimed bytes. Zoe — can you run repro with NVTX/rocTX scopes around the pager and the kernel selection path so we can correlate timestamps?

zoe: Yep — I'll run NVTX on H100 and ask Ajay to run rocTX on MI250X. Also adding kernel selection debug logs for tiling decisions.

ajay: I'll also try forcing smaller page granularity and see if it reduces fragmentation (--kv-page-size=64k). If that helps, we can consider an adaptive page-size heuristic.

evan: One more oddity: when I flip to legacy batching heuristics (disable continuous batching), the memory growth rate drops ~40%. That implies batching interacts with allocation patterns (batches that merge prefixes create hot spots).

rachel: Noted. That suggests we need cross-component test matrices (kernel selection x batching x page-size). Great catch.

evan: TL;DR action items:
- evan: add compaction trigger + reclaimed_bytes metric (WIP)
- zoe: run NVTX run + collect timeline (H100)
- ajay: reproduce on MI250X with rocprof, try --kv-page-size override
- rachel: prototype adaptive page-size heuristic and look at kernel selection metadata

pager-bot: eviction_threshold breached on staging worker-22 at 2025-07-12T15:09:00Z (auto-alert).

zoe: ACK. I'll upload the NVTX timeline to the perf bucket when done.

evan: If anyone sees a quick mitigation idea: temporarily limit reuse_window to 8 and force tiling_v2. That buys time while I work on compaction.

rachel: I'll run a small canary with those settings against the longctx test and report back.

ajay: Will post MI250X traces here once I have them.

evan: Thanks all — leaning toward a short-term config change + medium-term compaction/heuristic fix. Will follow up with a PR and a perf dashboard update. :thumbsup:
